## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED.**

### Finding 1 — a normative atom of the standby-settlement rule, and the successor of a declared `overwrite`, is carried by no document (RED)

*Symptom.* `portfolio_band_on_micro_market_settlements_a9b0c1ca.json` tells the reader, as law in force, "The settlement a client pays on each micro market in the Unattended Micro Market Program is discounted by a portfolio band that reads the client's whole market estate rather than the single site being invoiced", and then, under "## Scope of the discount", retires the only clause that bounded that discount: "The clause reading \"The discount is applied to the management fee and the equipment lease only; product cost, subsidy true-up, shrink adjustments and one-off charges carry no portfolio discount.\" is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis for a settlement raised for a period the market stood shut." The document named as the successor, `settlement_raised_for_a_period_a_market_stood_shut_99fb5cf8.json`, never states the successor semantics, and no other document does either.

*Root cause.* `market_ext_standby_period_settlement.rule` contains the sentence "No portfolio discount is taken off a settlement raised for a period the market stood shut, the standing charge and the fee share already reflecting that the market was not trading.", and `market_ext_standby_period_settlement.overwrite[0]` declares it the `replaced_by` of exactly the clause the KB retires. The render dropped it.

*Evidence.* A case-insensitive search for "portfolio" across all 67 documents returns three hits only: two in `micro_market_settlement_basis_and_pricing_tariff_efc2b5c8.json` (the printed ladder) and one in `portfolio_band_on_micro_market_settlements_a9b0c1ca.json` (the retirement notice). The string "No portfolio discount" occurs nowhere. `market.extended.yaml` was last written at 10:16 and the documents at 11:09, so the sentence was on the source side before the render ran.

*Why it bears on this task.* The retired clause was the only visible sentence saying that a subsidy true-up carries no portfolio discount. With it retired and no successor in sight, a reader of `portfolio_band_on_micro_market_settlements_a9b0c1ca.json` has a live rule that the settlement is discounted by a portfolio band and a closed four-amount assembly in `product_settlement_on_a_subsidy_true_up_basis_ff1e3341.json` that has no place for one; nothing published adjudicates. The scored numbers are untouched only because Pinehurst Analytics Group holds one micro market agreement and every format's ladder reads 0 per cent at one agreement — an accident of this seed, not a semantics the corpus carries. Under this skill this is recorded even where the numbers are unaffected.

*Affected documents and locations.* `env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/docs/market/portfolio_band_on_micro_market_settlements_a9b0c1ca.json`, section "## Scope of the discount"; `env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/docs/market/settlement_raised_for_a_period_a_market_stood_shut_99fb5cf8.json`, whole document.

*Relation to previous revisions.* This is revision 1 of this audit file; there is no earlier revision of the KB audit for this difficulty to compare against.

### Finding 2 — the published half-cent tie-break contradicts the source's own arithmetic at the one point where a tie occurs (policy-side; two scored arguments at risk)

*Symptom.* On this task's world the halved six-month discount is exactly 41.55 / 2 = 20.775, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent. The rule published in every computation document — "a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent" — resolves it to 20.78 and yields `settlement_amount_usd` 400.12 and `payment_amount_usd` 704.87. The scored values are 400.11 and 704.86.

*Root cause.* Policy side. The source binds `window_subsidy = RND(drawdowns_6m / 2, 2)` and `RND` is `lambda x, n=2: round(float(x), n)` (`skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py:388`); in binary floating point 41.55/2 is 20.774999…, so Python returns 20.77 — the odd cent, the opposite of the tie-break the same source publishes in `market_ext_period_settlement_true_up.rule`. The documents carry that rule text verbatim, so this is not a mistranslation.

*Evidence.* `market_ext_period_settlement_true_up.rule`: "The four amounts are each rounded to the nearest cent, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent as they are taken and are then added". `computations[1].factor_trace`: "41.55 over six months gives 20.77". `computations[1].expected` = 400.11; `computations[3].expected` = 704.86.

*Mitigation on the document side, recorded for completeness.* `product_settlement_on_a_subsidy_true_up_basis_ff1e3341.json` scopes its rounding to "**The four amounts** … and the sum", and the halved reading-window figure is not one of the four. A reader who rounds only those four reaches 20.775 × 97 per cent = 20.15175 → 20.15 and 20.775 / 20 per cent = 103.875 at 2.85 per cent = 2.96, giving 400.11 — the gold. So the corpus does entail the scored value, on the narrower reading. The five sibling computation documents all say "Each figure is rounded to the nearest cent … as it is taken" or "Every intermediate figure and the result are rounded", which is what led this auditor's blind derivation to the other reading. Because the openness is present in the source's own rule text in exactly the same form, it is recorded here as a policy-side note and does not by itself set this skill's verdict.

### Finding 4 — a declared retirement rendered at a narrower scope than the `overwrite` declares (minor rewrite)

*Symptom.* `monthly_settlement_terms_for_micro_markets_d597fee6.json` writes: "The clause reading \"Where sales for the period fall short of the sales guarantee printed against the market format, the shortfall share printed against that format is invoiced to the client; where sales exceed the guarantee, nothing further is invoiced and no rebate is given.\" is likewise **no longer in force on a subsidy true-up basis**." The `overwrite` declares the clause superseded without qualification: `{"base_policy": "market_settlement_terms", "superseded_clause": "Where sales for the period fall short …", "replaced_by": "No shortfall charge is invoiced on a subsidy true-up basis, …"}`.

*Root cause.* The render took the scope of the `replaced_by` sentence as the scope of the retirement, leaving the clause in force on commission and management-fee formats, which the source does not say.

*Why it is minor.* The extended policy that declares the overwrite is itself defined on the subsidy-true-up basis, so the narrowing is defensible and changes no number here: task 0's format settles on a subsidy true-up, where both readings agree. Recorded because the retired surface is judged as declared, not as implied.

*Affected document and location.* `env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/docs/market/monthly_settlement_terms_for_micro_markets_d597fee6.json`, section "## Shelf pricing and pass-throughs".

### Finding 5 — the ladders' "approved kiosk outage request" is never identified with the record the customer has (minor findability)

Eleven of this task's tiers turn on "approved kiosk outage requests"; the source binds every one of them to `COUNT('market_service_intake', …, request_type='service_credit_claim', request_status='approved')`. The records carry `request_type: 'service_credit_claim'`, and the `find_market_service_intake` schema calls them "service credit claims". No published sentence says the two are the same thing. `service_credits_for_micro_market_outages_77ee054e.json` comes closest — "Outage is measured from the approved market service requests on the agreement for that period" — and the titles carry the connection ("Client Service Credits for Kiosk Outage and Missed Restocking"), so the identification is inferable; but a reader works it out rather than reading it. Recorded as a findability omission on the factor side, not as a changed semantics — this auditor made the identification from the visible materials alone and reached every tier correctly.

The same document says outage is measured "for that period" while `working_the_credit_for_lost_kiosk_hours_f64597ba.json` and `how_far_back_approved_outage_hours_are_read_ff671094.json` read the hours over a three-, six- or twelve-month window to the day the credit is worked out. The base clause and the extended reading window are not reconciled in prose; the extended policy governs, and no number turns on it here.

### Finding 7 — "the settlement charges" is never defined against the records (policy-side openness, recorded, not a document defect)

Three quantities of this task — the charge-reading window of the tender, the settlement the outage credit is applied to, and the count that decides the charge-reading tier — read "the settlement charges" or "the settlement charged on the agreement". The source binds all of them to `SUM('market_ledger','amount_usd', …, event_type='market_monthly_settlement_invoiced')`, which takes equipment lines and monthly settlement charges alike; the gold settlement base of 1762.26 is "the July equipment line of 480.00, the July settlement of 402.15, the August equipment line of 480.00 and the August product settlement of 400.11". A reader who instead takes "settlement charge" to be only what the two settlement tools post — which `invoicing_the_product_settlement_of_a_micro_market_dc20787d.json` calls "a single monthly settlement charge … where it joins the equipment line" — reaches an outage credit of 93.27 and a tender of 0.00 on this world, at which two declared factors stop moving the figure. The source's own rule text carries exactly the same openness ("the settlement charges read over that window"), so under this skill it is a policy-side note and the documents may not close what the source leaves open.

### Summary of the verdict

`KB-BIJECTION RED` on finding 1. Findings 2, 5 and 7 are policy-side or minor and do not by themselves set the verdict; finding 4 is a minor rewrite on the retired surface, recorded with its location. Everything else in the domain of this task's four extended policies and the eleven base policies — every baseline default, every tier of all nineteen declared factor ladders including the untriggered ones, every `overwrite`, every tool contract and both prerequisite sentences of the root problem — corresponds losslessly at the level of entailment.
